children.name: Summary
children.text: NaN counts once. Objects match only by reference.

children.name: Text
children.text: I want to learn Set properly. I use it, but I'm not sure of the rules.

children.name: Text
children.text: Good place to start. Set has six concepts, and you have passed one. Before I explain anything, one quick check.

children.name: Text
children.text: The two NaN were right to merge. The miss was the objects. A Set treats two objects as equal only if they are the same object, not if they look the same.

children.name: Text
children.text: A Set also keeps the order values were first added. Put these lines in order.

children.name: Text
children.text: Now put both rules to work.

children.name: Text
children.text: Does has() use the same rule?

children.name: Text
children.text: Yes. add, has and delete all use the same rule.

children.name: Text
children.text: Close. The failing test keeps a later duplicate. Line 8 asks seen about each key. Which line adds a key to seen?
